summary: [standards] One owner per pass condition is broken for a document that is not an envelope: L0.contract-version walks documents_of_json_runs (any JSON value) instead of envelopes(), so its `markers-present` condition fires on a document with no `meta` object. checker.md row L0.contract-version says `every envelope`; L0.envelope owns a document that is not one. Reproduced: fake tool whose `team add --json` prints {"ok":true,"data":{}} fails both L0.envelope (`meta is a required property`) and L0.contract-version (`meta has no contract and contractVersion`), so a single seeded violation fails two MUST checks. The same holds for a probe that prints `[1]` or {"foo":1} (L0.envelope, L0.contract-version, L0.json-mode-preparse, L0.no-env-switch; the last two are legitimate owners of their own rules). The seeded set (atip_check_56) has no case for a document without meta, so the check passes the brief's `one violation, one owner` claim without covering this one. Fix: judge contract-version on envelopes() (is_envelope documents) only, and add a seeded case. Blast radius: every tool that prints a document without `meta` gets a second MUST failure, which hides which rule the author broke.
